_comment: Roots for scripts/check_reachability.py, and the baseline it ratchets.
MOST ROOTS ARE DERIVED, not listed here: a decorated function, a method overriding a base
defined outside boltrig/, module-level code, a dunder, and a getattr with a literal string.
This file is for the rest - a process entry point, a CLI, a handler a config names by
string - and it is the honest weak point of the whole check. An over-broad root set
silently re-admits the defect the check exists to catch, so every entry needs a reason
naming WHAT calls it and HOW.
THE ROOT SET IS DELIBERATELY EMPTY ON THIS FIRST RUN. 145 functions are unreachable and 71
of them have no caller at all, and that raw number is more useful than a number laundered
through a list of roots someone guessed at in an afternoon. Declaring a root is how the
count falls, and each declaration is a claim a reader can check. So is deleting the
function, which for a good share of these 71 is the right answer. The first two the report
named, `redact` in kernel/pii.py and `apply_rls` in store/postgres.py, have now been looked
at, and they turned out to be different cases - which is the argument for looking rather
than batch-declaring. `apply_rls` is an OPERATOR action, correctly having no in-package
caller, and is declared below. `redact` is a genuine overclaim and is recorded in
unwired-claims-allow.json with a blocker, having taken SEC-13's description down with it.
The 71 include every name the repaired unwired-claims gate reports and every name its
waiver file waives, which is the corroboration that the graph is measuring what it claims:
select_or_generate_workflow, sweep_run_scoped, execute_write, push, consume, accept_once,
build_cell_scope, dev_principal_resolver, select_locale and store_bearer_verifier are all
here, arrived at from the other direction.

roots.apply_rls: An OPERATOR action, not an application call, and its own docstring says so: it applies the opt-in RLS overlay (boltrig/store/rls.sql) and is explicitly NOT run by default, because the owner-connected default path relies on the per-method `WHERE tenant_id = $1` filter (SEC-08). A deployment that wants DB-enforced isolation runs it once, then connects as `boltrig_app` and uses `with_tenant`. Having no in-package caller is the correct shape for it: a call site would mean the application applying its own database grants. It is exercised end to end by tests/integration/test_rls.py:64, which is the check that the SQL it runs is real rather than the operator's problem.
roots.canonical_device_action: DeviceLeaseIssuer in boltrig/device_leases.py calls this validator for every dispatcher and approval action. The reachability scanner deliberately excludes top-level boltrig/*.py modules, so that real call is outside its derived graph; declaring the validator also reaches its digest and relative-path helpers.
roots.set_budget: Fleet-manifest seeding calls the InMemoryStore or PostgresStore compatibility method through `_seed_call(store, "set_budget", ...)` in boltrig/config/manifest.py because the two implementations are respectively synchronous and asynchronous. The variable-backed getattr is deliberately invisible to the static call graph; both implementations forward to the canonical budget-policy state.
roots.canonical_camera_action: CameraLeaseIssuer in boltrig/camera_leases.py calls this validator for every camera action it issues a lease for (lines 139 and 189). Exactly the shape of canonical_device_action above: the reachability scanner deliberately excludes top-level boltrig/*.py, so its only callers are invisible to it. Declaring it also reaches its two private helpers, _angle and _camera_id, which nothing else calls.
roots.get_camera_binding: Called as self._store.get_camera_binding by CameraLeaseIssuer (boltrig/camera_leases.py:144) through the store protocol. The call site is in an excluded top-level module and the dispatch is by protocol, so neither end is visible to a static walk. The Postgres and in-memory stores implement it as a pair; this root covers the implementation the scanner reports.
roots.create_camera_lease: Called as self._store.create_camera_lease by CameraLeaseIssuer (boltrig/camera_leases.py:229) when a lease is granted. Same excluded-caller and protocol-dispatch shape as get_camera_binding.
roots.list_owner_bindings: Re-exported into the device surface: boltrig/kernel/device_routes.py:20 imports it as list_owner_camera_bindings and registers it there, and boltrig/kernel/camera_agent_routes.py names it in its own __all__. A re-export under an alias is a call the scanner cannot follow.
roots.build_deepgram: The adapter loader resolves this factory from the manifest string `boltrig.adapters.builtin.cloud_audio:build_deepgram`; both manifest.yaml and manifest.example.yaml declare that exact module_ref. String-named adapter factories are runtime roots that the static call graph cannot derive.
roots.build_elevenlabs: The adapter loader resolves this factory from the manifest string `boltrig.adapters.builtin.cloud_audio:build_elevenlabs`; both manifest.yaml and manifest.example.yaml declare that exact module_ref.
